home.title: Games for learning Armenian words
home.lead: The lexicon is merged from Arahet's teaching items and a thematic vocabulary of 2000 words. Fifteen themes, four levels, fourteen games — from pair matching to writing from memory.
home.artDescription: Placeholder art instead of a mascot: the mascot is planned for the second version.
home.contentsSub: The board games have their own field; the round games share one question shape, a timer and five lives.
home.screenSub: Own field and own life cycle
home.roundSub: Shared question shape, timer and five lives
home.auditBody: There is no application code yet, only the plan. The lexicon is not imported, the audio is not copied, and no recording has been checked by a native speaker. The text size already works — it is driven by a single CSS variable.

settings.title: Reading
settings.intro: The text size applies immediately. The remaining settings arrive with the local progress store.
settings.textHint: Six steps. Every text size in the app changes, captions included.
settings.voiceHint: Two speakers from one Piper model. The choice changes the timbre, not the quality: both versions are synthetic.
settings.voicePending: The voice becomes available once the audio is imported.
settings.audioHint: The switch removes the listen buttons for unreviewed recordings instead of silencing them. The synthetic-audio note stays either way.
settings.dataHint: Progress is stored on this device only. There is no file export yet, and clearing the app data deletes it for good.

about.title: Пружинки
about.bodyFirst: The name is թունջիկ, a diminutive of թունջ “to jump”, so “the hopping toy”. The Russian “Пружинки” is a playful gloss after the image of a spring toy, not a literal translation.
about.bodySecond: This app does not replace the Arahet course, it trains its lexicon differently: not “finish a lesson” but “practise what you know”. Its progress is separate — Arahet's progress is neither read nor updated.
about.bodyThird: The visual system is shared with Arahet: the same paper, the same typefaces, the same grid. What differs is the accent — ochre instead of rust — and the fact that the reward is drawn rather than pasted in as emoji.
about.sourceBody: The lexicon is merged from Arahet's registry and the vocabulary of the aybuch project. The audio is synthesised with the hy_AM-tigran_nune-medium model, distributed under GPL-2.0; the right to distribute the generated clips has not been verified and remains a release blocker.
